title: Adaptive DType Pathfinder with Calibration Guardrails
creator: Priya Singh
description:
Why: We need a low-risk, production-safe mechanism for selecting between FP16, FP8, and INT8 execution lanes at inference time that preserves latency SLOs while preventing silent quality regressions. Current approaches are brittle: wide per-layer switches can cause unpredictable accuracy drops or latency spikes when models see out-of-distribution inputs.

What: Design and implement an "Adaptive DType Pathfinder" — a runtime component that observes short online micro-profiles of incoming request batches, consults compact per-layer sensitivity signatures produced by calibration, and chooses an execution lane (FP16/FP8/INT8 hybrid) that satisfies a configurable accuracy headroom and latency budget. The Pathfinder includes two guardrail mechanisms: 1) shadow validation (fast lightweight executors run on a small sample and compare outputs) and 2) conservative rolling windows that prevent rapid lane flips for noisy workloads.

Scope: This ticket covers the Pathfinder control logic, integration points with the calibration artifact store (quant-profiles), the shadow-validation harness, telemetry and decision logging, and a minimal rollback/fallback primitive. Kernel-level execution primitives will be invoked via the existing runtime API; this PR does not reimplement low-level kernels.

Key ideas and novel aspects: compact per-layer sensitivity fingerprints (statistical delta signatures) instead of full calibration tables; fast runtime probing that piggybacks on normal batching to avoid extra GPU work; shadow validation that runs on a tiny subset of requests (1-5%) on a best-effort lane to verify accuracy assumptions; and a confidence-weighted blending policy that allows partial-layer downgrades for tolerant submodules (attention vs MLP).

Non-goals: Model distillation, retraining, or long offline calibration jobs. Full multi-tenant scheduler policy changes are out-of-scope for this ticket.
acceptance_criteria: Pathfinder selects an execution lane (FP16/FP8/INT8 or hybrid) for incoming request batches based on per-batch micro-profiles and stored quant-profiles
Shadow validation runs on a sampled subset and reports per-request delta metrics to telemetry without adding >2% tail latency to sampled requests
Rolling window prevents lane oscillation: no more than 1 lane change per route per 30s under steady load
Decision logs include reason codes and a pointer to the quant-profile version used (for postmortem and audits)
Automated acceptance harness demonstrates <=1.5% relative drop in beam-averaged quality compared to FP16 baseline on curated eval prompts when using conservative headroom settings
Integration tests cover failure modes: if shadow validation fails repeatedly, runtime falls back to FP16 within 3 attempts and emits an alert metric
comments: 2026-02-22 Priya Singh: Initial scoping complete. Prototype approach uses per-layer 64-bit signatures derived from calibration sample histograms. Will schedule design review with Applied ML next week.

2026-02-28 Miguel Ortega: Reviewed proposed signature format. Concern: signatures must be stable across minor model updates. Suggest embedding model-version hash and calibration-seed in the quant-profile metadata.
2026-03-03 Design review notes (Asha Patel): prefer visualizing lane-retry rates in Console rollout view. Add a small UI hook to expose recent Pathfinder decisions for a route.

2026-03-07 Liam Chen: Initial prototype implemented: micro-profiling piggybacks on the first token batch; shadow validation implemented as a lightweight fused-kernel path that copies outputs to host for delta computation. Benchmarks attached.

2026-03-10 QA: Shadow sampling at 3% shows 1.2% median latency overhead on p3-standard tests; tail p99 overhead is within 2.1% — acceptable for canary. Two cases of oscillation observed on synthetic bursty traffic; extended rolling window to 30s fixed it.
2026-03-12 Security: Confirmed that decision logs do not contain raw model outputs; only hashed signatures and numeric deltas are stored. Approved for behavioral telemetry collection.
2026-03-14 Priya Singh: Preparing rollout plan for canary on runtime-2.4 in us-west-2 with feature flag. Next: tie failure-triggered alerts into runbooks and automated fallback policy.
